title: Mali Care: Workforce planning
stem:
All organizations and data in this question are fictional.

Mali Care: Mali provides home care. Its district’s population is ageing, and public transport no longer runs late enough for evening visits.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Define the term human resource planning.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Explain two factors affecting human resource planning at Mali Care.

steps.text: Forecasting the number and skills of employees required
and planning how the organization will obtain, develop and retain those people.
An ageing population can increase demand for care.
Mali may need more carers and specialist skills in supporting older adults.
Failing to plan for that demand can leave evening visits unfilled.
Reduced transport limits labour mobility.
Potential carers without cars cannot reach late visits.
Mali may need transport support or different schedules to secure an adequate evening workforce.

All organizations and data in this question are fictional.

Nru Hotels: Nru proposes a single-union and no-strike agreement in return for regular bargaining and independent dispute resolution. Several staff fear losing their strongest bargaining tool.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Define the term collective bargaining.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage for Nru Hotels of using the proposed negotiated settlement.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Using the case information and relevant business management theory, recommend whether Nru Hotels should proceed with using the proposed negotiated settlement.

steps.text: Negotiation between an employer and employee representatives
to agree employment terms or resolve workplace issues collectively.
Advantage: Predictable dispute procedures can reduce service disruption.
Applied consequence: Nru can protect bookings while providing regular employee representation.
Disadvantage: Employees surrender some industrial leverage.
Applied consequence: a no-strike agreement may weaken pressure if management delays addressing concerns.
Indicative support: Predictable dispute procedures can reduce service disruption because Nru can protect bookings while providing regular employee representation
Indicative counterargument: Employees surrender some industrial leverage because a no-strike agreement may weaken pressure if management delays addressing concerns

One defensible judgment: Proceed only with credible timelines, independent resolution and meaningful bargaining rights; a one-sided restriction may intensify distrust. Alternative recommendations earn full credit when supported by the case and a coherent response to the counterargument.

Evidence limitation: The independence and enforcement of the proposed dispute mechanism are unspecified. Explain how this uncertainty affects confidence in the decision. Apply best fit: a theoretical-only answer can earn at most 4; without an explained case/stimulus limitation at most 8. Do not require all indicative points or award them separately.

Accurate relevant theory supports balanced, developed analysis of using the proposed negotiated settlement using the specific circumstances of Nru Hotels. The recommendation follows from the arguments and recognizes a condition or stakeholder trade-off.

Focused, balanced analysis integrates relevant business theory with the evidence about Nru Hotels; competing consequences and their relative significance are evaluated. The recommendation is convincing and conditional, addresses an identified weakness, and explains a material limitation of the available evidence.
